The shared phase4_build.zig entrypoint already keeps the runtime atomic64 gate and the bitmap gate in the same replay path, which is the current measurable rollback surface for local and CI runs.

The validation matrix already names the rollback owner, the exact `threshold_pending_until_runtime_atomic64_scope_widens` threshold posture, and the reversible-delivery evidence for the live runtime atomic64 gate, so the atomic64 survey should point at that published ownership note instead of repeating it loosely.

The Phase 4 roadmap still names zigux/tests/atomic64_diff.zig, but the shipped tree uses zigux/tests/runtime_atomic64_diff.zig. The next bounded step is to choose one canonical path and update the roadmap-facing note in the same change before anyone claims a broader atomic64 diff surface.

The live gate is still a bounded rollback-readiness slice. It covers exchange, cmpxchg, add_unless, inc_not_zero, dec_if_positive, selftest-family lifecycle, and post-selftest replay checks, but it does not claim the full wider atomic64_test.c surface, and the published Phase 4 matrix still records `threshold_pending_until_runtime_atomic64_scope_widens` instead of any approved perf threshold.
